title: Flat monomorphisms of algebraic spaces are representable by schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; locally finite type is the chart test with [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat and a monomorphism, meaning that $X(H)\to Y(H)$ is injective for every $S$-scheme $H$. Then $f$ is representable by schemes: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to Y$, the sheaf $X\times_Yh_T$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. No finite-type, finite-presentation or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme test $h_T\to Y$ and put $Z=X\times_Yh_T$. This is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and $Z\to h_T$ is flat by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. On each test scheme, two pairs in $Z$ with the same $T$-component have equal $X$-components by monomorphy of $f$; thus this projection is a monomorphism. Cover $T$ by affine opens $T_j$. The inverse images $Z_j$ are open subspaces covering $Z$. By [lem-sfb-space-largest-schematic-open], once each $Z_j$ is a scheme, they all lie in the largest schematic open of $Z$, which therefore has full point image and so is all of $Z$ [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. It suffices to treat $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}B$.

By [lem-a1-space-affine-atlas-open-cover], cover $Z$ by open subspaces $W$ admitting surjective etale maps from affine schemes. Each $|W|$ is quasi-compact, being the continuous image of the quasi-compact affine atlas; continuity is [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The restriction $q:W\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is flat: every etale scheme chart of $W$ is also an etale chart of $Z$, so its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is flat. It is still a monomorphism. Its diagonal is an isomorphism, since on every test scheme a pair with equal images consists of two equal elements. In particular its diagonal is quasi-compact, so $q$ is quasi-separated. The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is quasi-separated (its affine structure map is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]). By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], $q$ is quasi-compact. As before, [lem-sfb-space-largest-schematic-open] reduces schemehood of $Z$ to schemehood of all these $W$.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-schemehood-local-ring-test] to the quasi-compact quasi-separated $q:W\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. For each $w\in|W|$ with image $t$, set $A=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B,t}$ and $P=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}A$. The map $r:P\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat and quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] and [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. It remains a monomorphism by the pair calculation of step 1. Choose a field-valued representative $\operatorname{Spec}K\to W$ of $w$. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ hits $t$, so the ring map $B\to K$ factors through $A=B_t$ and has kernel $tA$ there. The resulting compatible pair gives a point $p\in|P|$ over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Proving each such $P$ a scheme proves $W$ a scheme.

Since $r$ is quasi-compact and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, $P$ is quasi-compact [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]: it admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme. Cover that scheme by finitely many affine opens; their disjoint union is an affine scheme $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] with a representable surjective etale map $u:U\to P$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $|u|$ is surjective, so some $y\in U$ maps to the point $p$ of step 3. By the chart test of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], applied to the charts $u$ and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the scheme morphism $v=r\circ u:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat, and $v(y)$ is the closed point. Every prime of the local ring $A$ is contained in its maximal ideal, hence every point $s$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ specializes to the closed point. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] some $y\prime\in U$ has $v(y\prime)=s$. Hence $v$ is surjective, and so is $r$ on point classes.

The flat surjective morphism $v:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of affine schemes forms an fpqc covering $\{v\}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: an affine open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a finite union of standard opens $D(a)$, and $v^{-1}(D(a))$ is a standard, hence affine, open of $U$ mapping onto $D(a)$ by surjectivity. Form $P\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}U$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] with its projection to $U$. On a test scheme $H$, a pair $(z,y)\in P(H)\times U(H)$ with $r(z)=v(y)=r(u(y))$ has $z=u(y)$ by monomorphy of $r$ (step 3); so $y\mapsto(u(y),y)$ is inverse to the projection, which is an isomorphism. Thus $P\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}U$ is represented by the scheme $U$ and its projection is an open immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-open-immersion-descent] with $Z=P$, base scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$, $a=r$ and the covering $\{v\}$: $r$ identifies $P$ with an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. That open contains every point because $r$ is surjective (step 4), so it is $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $P$ is represented by the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

The local-ring criterion in step 3 now makes each $W$ a scheme. The largest schematic opens used in steps 2 and 1 then give, successively, schemehood over every affine $T_j$ and schemehood of $Z=X\times_Yh_T$. Since $T$ and its map to $Y$ were arbitrary, this is representability by schemes. All quasi-compactness hypotheses were introduced only for the covering pieces $W$; none was required of the original $f$.
